Create stacked taxa bar chart showing relative abundance in each culture
read in .txt file that we got from omics box
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Start with a clean slate
rm(list=ls())

taxo <- read.table("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/kraken/gtdbtk/taxonomic_classification.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, fill = TRUE)

```

Filter for genus level only
```{r}
taxo_genus <- taxo[taxo$Rank == "genus", ]
```


Calculate percentages
```{r}

taxo_data <- taxo_genus[, -c(1, 2, 3)]  # Remove the Rank, TaxId, and Scientific Name columns (adjust column indexes if necessary)

# Calculate column sums (total abundance per sample)
col_sums <- colSums(taxo_data)

# Calculate percentage relative to each sample (i.e., normalize columns)
taxo_percentage <- sweep(taxo_data, 2, col_sums, FUN = "/") * 100

#to check that percentages are being calculated correctly
#taxo_percentage["Total", ] <- colSums(taxo_percentage, na.rm = TRUE)

#taxo_percentage$Total1 <- rowSums(taxo_percentage, na.rm = TRUE)



```

Apply 1% threshold so that anything that is less than 1% of the population will be put into other
```{r}
# Identify values < 1%
low_abundance_mask <- taxo_percentage < 1

# Calculate "Other" row
other_row <- colSums(taxo_percentage * low_abundance_mask, na.rm = TRUE)

# Set those low values to zero
taxo_percentage[low_abundance_mask] <- 0

# Filter out rows where everything is now 0 (they're fully below 1%)
keep_rows <- rowSums(taxo_percentage) > 0
taxo_percentage_filtered <- taxo_percentage[keep_rows, ]
taxo_metadata_filtered <- taxo_genus[keep_rows, c(1, 2, 3)]

# Add metadata back to filtered data
taxo_filtered <- cbind(taxo_metadata_filtered, taxo_percentage_filtered)

# Build the "Other" row
other_row_df <- data.frame(
  Rank = "genus",
  TaxId = NA,
  Scientific.Name = "Other",
  t(other_row)
)
colnames(other_row_df) <- colnames(taxo_filtered)

# Combine with "Other"
taxo_filtered <- rbind(taxo_filtered, other_row_df)

# Remove Planktothrix before reshaping for plotting
taxo_filtered <- taxo_filtered[taxo_filtered$Scientific.Name != "Planktothrix", ]


```


After removing Planktothrix, normalize the data so the total abundance for each sample reaches 100%
```{r}

# For each sample, calculate the sum of the abundance values (after removing Planktothrix)
sample_sums <- colSums(taxo_filtered[, -c(1, 2, 3)], na.rm = TRUE)

# Normalize the abundance values so they sum to 100% per sample
taxo_filtered[, -c(1, 2, 3)] <- sweep(taxo_filtered[, -c(1, 2, 3)], 2, sample_sums, FUN = "/") * 100

```

Create stacked bar chart
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggsci)

# Define 21 distinct, visually accessible colors
my_colors <- c(
  "#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#e7298a", "#66a61e",
  "#e6ab02", "#a6761d", "#666666", "#1f78b4", "#b2df8a",
  "#fb9a99", "#fdbf6f", "#cab2d6", "#ffff99", "#b15928",
  "#8dd3c7", "#ffffb3", "#bebada", "#fb8072", "#80b1d3",
  "#fdb462", "#bc80bd", "#ccebc5", "#ffed6f","#e41a1c", "#377eb8"
)


# Create the stacked bar chart
ggplot(taxo_long, aes(x = Abundance, y = Sample, fill = Scientific.Name)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors) +
  labs(x = "Relative Abundance (%)",
       y = expression(italic("Planktothrix") ~ "isolate designation"),  # expression italics
       fill = "Genus") +   
  theme_minimal() +
   theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 10),   
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),                          
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),                         
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8)                           
  )


#save
ggsave("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/bar_charts/stacked_bar_chart_gtdbtk2.png", width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```

############################### create a total abundance chart
This should be how many times we see each unique genus across all cultures, what are we most likely to see? Genus on x axis

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Remove TaxId and filter out Planktothrix
taxo_genus_filtered <- taxo_genus %>%
  dplyr::select(-TaxId)

# 2. Calculate total abundance per genus
genus_abundance <- taxo_genus_filtered %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Total_Abundance = sum(c_across(-c(Rank, Scientific.Name)))) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Compute total abundance across all genera
total_all <- sum(genus_abundance$Total_Abundance)

# 4. Filter out genera that contribute less than 1%
genus_above_1pct <- genus_abundance %>%
 mutate(Percent_Total = (Total_Abundance / total_all) * 100) %>% #to make it a percent
  filter(Percent_Total >= 1, # now filtering on 1%
         Scientific.Name != "Planktothrix") %>% #remove Planktothrix
  mutate(
    Phylum = case_when(
      Scientific.Name %in% c("JJ008", "Flavobacterium") ~ "Bacteroidota",
      TRUE ~ "Pseudomonadota"
    )
  )

genus_above_1pct <- genus_above_1pct %>%
  mutate(Scientific.Name = recode(Scientific.Name,
                                  "Kinneretia" = "JACDQM01 (Kinneretia)"))

# 5. Plot
ggplot(genus_above_1pct,
       aes(x = reorder(Scientific.Name, -Total_Abundance),
           y = Percent_Total,
           fill = Phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "Genus",
       y = "Total Abundance (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pseudomonadota" = "#66C2A6",
                               "Bacteroidota" = "#FD8D63")) 


ggsave("F:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/bar_charts/most_abundant_genus.png", width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```


Stats: is the community uniform or different across the cultures?
(beta diversity/community composition)
```{r}
#--------------------------------------- prep abundance matrix --------------------------------------------
# use taxo_percentage again so that we haven't filtered into an other column yet, we want all genus present
taxo_percentage <- sweep(taxo_data, 2, colSums(taxo_data), FUN = "/") * 100 #had to write this again because we wrote over it earlier

# Convert to long format for creating a matrix
abundance_long <- taxo_percentage %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(Scientific.Name = taxo_genus$Scientific.Name) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Scientific.Name, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Abundance")

# Pivot to get samples as rows, genera as columns
abundance_matrix <- abundance_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Scientific.Name, values_from = Abundance, values_fill = 0)

# Convert to data.frame (tibble can't have rownames)
abundance_matrix <- as.data.frame(abundance_matrix)

# Set rownames from the Sample column
rownames(abundance_matrix) <- abundance_matrix$Sample

# Remove Sample column
abundance_matrix <- abundance_matrix[, -1]

#need to rename samples for grouping later in PERMANOVA step
sample_name_map <- c(
  "Trim135115_CCACAACA.GTACCACA_S55" = "1810",
  "Trim135108_CGGCATTA.GTCAGTCA_S48" = "1031",
  "Trim135109_CACGCAAT.CCTTCCAT_S49" = "1033",
  "Trim135110_GGAATGTC.AGGAACAC_S50" = "1809",
  "Trim135112_GGACATCA.TACCTGCA_S52" = "1025",
  "Trim135113_GGTGTACA.AGACGCTA_S53" = "1027",
  "Trim135114_GATAGCCA.CAACACAG_S54" = "1808",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4" = "1026",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1029" = "1029",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1030" = "1030",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1032" = "1032",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1801" = "1801",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1802" = "1802",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1803" = "1803",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1804" = "1804",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1805" = "1805",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1806" = "1806",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1807" = "1807",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1811" = "1811",
  "TrimHH3VGDSXY_s4_1812" = "1812"
)

# Apply mapping
rownames(abundance_matrix) <- sample_name_map[rownames(abundance_matrix)]

#--------------------------------------- create grouping factor --------------------------------------------
# Group by 10xx vs 18xx series
sample_group <- ifelse(grepl("^10", rownames(abundance_matrix)), "10xx", "18xx")
sample_group <- factor(sample_group)

#--------------------------------------- Bray-Curtis & PERMANOVA --------------------------------------------
library(vegan)

# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
dist_bc <- vegdist(abundance_matrix, method = "bray")

# PERMANOVA
set.seed(42)
permanova_res <- adonis2(dist_bc ~ sample_group, permutations = 999)
permanova_res


#the 10xx series has 3 outliers making the two groups "technically" different but most are clustering together
#the below check is with outliers removed
#--------------------------------------- bray-curtis dissimilarity --------------------------------------------

# Remove outlier samples
abundance_matrix_no_outliers <- abundance_matrix[!(rownames(abundance_matrix) %in% c("1030","1031","1032")), ]

# Update sample group
sample_group_no_outliers <- ifelse(grepl("^10", rownames(abundance_matrix_no_outliers)), "10xx", "18xx")
sample_group_no_outliers <- factor(sample_group_no_outliers)

# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity without outliers
dist_bc_no_outliers <- vegdist(abundance_matrix_no_outliers, method = "bray")

# PERMANOVA without outliers
set.seed(42)
permanova_res_no_outliers <- adonis2(dist_bc_no_outliers ~ sample_group_no_outliers, permutations = 999)
permanova_res_no_outliers


```

NMDS with grouping
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

#-----------------------------------
# Run NMDS if not already done
nmds_result <- metaMDS(abundance_matrix, distance = "bray", k = 2, trymax = 100)

# Extract coordinates
nmds_coords <- as.data.frame(nmds_result$points)
nmds_coords$Sample <- rownames(abundance_matrix)

# Add grouping information
nmds_coords$Group <- sample_group[rownames(nmds_coords)]

#-----------------------------------
# Plot NMDS colored by sample_group
ggplot(nmds_coords, aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = Group, label = Sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "NMDS of Cultures (Bray-Curtis)",
       subtitle = "Colored by 10xx vs 18xx groups",
       x = "NMDS1", y = "NMDS2") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("10xx" = "#1b9e77", "18xx" = "#d95f02")) +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10))

```

Which genus are causing the outliers
```{r}
# Mean abundance per genus
genus_means <- colMeans(abundance_matrix)

# Extract the outlier samples
outliers <- abundance_matrix[c("1030", "1031", "1032"), ]

# Calculate difference from the mean for each genus
diff_from_mean <- sweep(outliers, 2, genus_means, FUN = "-")

# View top genera that deviate the most in each outlier
top_diff_1030_named <- sort(unlist(diff_from_mean["1030", ]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top_diff_1031_named <- sort(unlist(diff_from_mean["1031", ]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
top_diff_1032_named <- sort(unlist(diff_from_mean["1032", ]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

top_diff_1030_named
top_diff_1031_named
top_diff_1032_named

```



Look for any unique species before applying 1% threshold
```{r}
# Combine percentages with metadata
taxo_with_meta <- cbind(
  taxo_genus[, c("Rank", "TaxId", "Scientific.Name")],  # metadata
  taxo_percentage
)

# Create presence matrix: anything > 0 is considered present
presence_matrix <- taxo_with_meta[, -c(1,2,3)] > 0

# Count in how many samples each genus appears
sample_counts <- rowSums(presence_matrix)

# ------------------------------
# 1. Unique genera: appear in exactly 1 sample
# ------------------------------
unique_genera <- taxo_with_meta[sample_counts == 1, ]
unique_genera$Unique_to <- apply(presence_matrix[sample_counts == 1, ], 1, function(x) {
  colnames(presence_matrix)[which(x)]
})

# ------------------------------
# 2. Shared genera: appear in more than 1 but not all samples
# ------------------------------
num_samples <- ncol(presence_matrix)
shared_genera <- taxo_with_meta[sample_counts > 1 & sample_counts < num_samples, ]

# ------------------------------
# 3. Core genera: appear in all samples
# ------------------------------
core_genera <- taxo_with_meta[sample_counts == num_samples, ]

# ------------------------------
# Outputs
# ------------------------------
cat("Number of unique genera:", nrow(unique_genera), "\n")
cat("Number of shared genera:", nrow(shared_genera), "\n")
cat("Number of core genera:", nrow(core_genera), "\n")

# Optional: view results
head(unique_genera)
head(shared_genera)
head(core_genera)

```


Look for unique species for only genus >1% abundance
This wound up being zero, everything above 1% is in all cultures
```{r}

# Combine metadata with genus-level percentages
taxo_for_presence <- cbind(
  taxo_genus[, c("Rank", "TaxId", "Scientific.Name")],
  taxo_percentage  # original percentages, not thresholded
)

# Optional: remove Planktothrix
taxo_for_presence <- taxo_for_presence[taxo_for_presence$Scientific.Name != "Planktothrix", ]

# Create presence/absence matrix: TRUE if abundance > 0
presence_matrix_full <- taxo_for_presence[, -c(1,2,3)] > 0

# Count how many samples each genus appears in
sample_counts_full <- rowSums(presence_matrix_full)

# Number of samples
num_samples <- ncol(presence_matrix_full)

# Identify genera that reach ≥1% in at least one sample
taxa_over_1perc <- rowSums(taxo_for_presence[, -c(1,2,3)] >= 1) > 0

# ------------------------------
# 1. Unique genera: exactly 1 sample AND ≥1% somewhere
# ------------------------------
unique_idx <- (sample_counts_full == 1) & taxa_over_1perc
unique_genera_1perc_any <- taxo_for_presence[unique_idx, ]

# Add column showing which sample contains the unique genus
unique_genera_1perc_any$Unique_to <- apply(presence_matrix_full[unique_idx, ], 1, function(x) {
  colnames(presence_matrix_full)[which(x)]
})

# ------------------------------
# 2. Shared genera: >1 and < all samples AND ≥1% somewhere
# ------------------------------
shared_idx <- (sample_counts_full > 1 & sample_counts_full < num_samples) & taxa_over_1perc
shared_genera_1perc_any <- taxo_for_presence[shared_idx, ]

# ------------------------------
# 3. Core genera: present in all samples AND ≥1% somewhere
# ------------------------------
core_idx <- (sample_counts_full == num_samples) & taxa_over_1perc
core_genera_1perc_any <- taxo_for_presence[core_idx, ]

# ------------------------------
# Check counts
# ------------------------------
cat("Number of unique genera:", nrow(unique_genera_1perc_any), "\n")
cat("Number of shared genera:", nrow(shared_genera_1perc_any), "\n")
cat("Number of core genera:", nrow(core_genera_1perc_any), "\n")



```


Which genus is the most abundant and how much more abundant is it
```{r}
# Exclude Planktothrix
taxo_no_plankt_counts <- taxo_genus[taxo_genus$Scientific.Name != "Planktothrix", ]

# 1. Calculate total raw counts per genus across all samples
taxo_no_plankt_counts$Total_Abundance <- rowSums(taxo_no_plankt_counts[, -c(1,2,3)])

# 2. Identify the most abundant genus
most_abundant_idx <- which.max(taxo_no_plankt_counts$Total_Abundance)
most_abundant_genus <- taxo_no_plankt_counts$Scientific.Name[most_abundant_idx]
most_abundance_value <- taxo_no_plankt_counts$Total_Abundance[most_abundant_idx]

# 3. Compare to the second most abundant genus
taxo_sorted <- taxo_no_plankt_counts[order(-taxo_no_plankt_counts$Total_Abundance), ]
second_most_abundance <- taxo_sorted$Total_Abundance[2]
difference <- most_abundance_value - second_most_abundance
fold_difference <- most_abundance_value / second_most_abundance

# 4. Output results
cat("Most abundant genus (excluding Planktothrix):", most_abundant_genus, "\n")
cat("Total abundance (sum of raw counts across samples):", most_abundance_value, "\n")
cat("Second most abundant genus:", taxo_sorted$Scientific.Name[2], "\n")
cat("Difference in abundance:", difference, "\n")
cat("Fold difference:", round(fold_difference, 2), "times more abundant\n")

```
